scope: Original Nano JPEG candidates only; proposed bilingual goals and all three full prompts read. All three 2752x1536 originals visually inspected at original detail. Formulas independently derived and numerical examples recalculated. This is not OCR-only validation and does not import or approve canonical assets.
independence: No generator outputs or other reviewers' scripts informed the first visual decisions. Root subsequently confirmed the same findings. Earlier B040r synthesis is a separate nonblind task.

formulaChecks.doubleSlit: Normally incident equal-phase sources: Δs≈d sinθ; constructive phases require mλ, destructive phases require (m+1/2)λ. Screen geometry y=L tanθ; y≈L sinθ only at small angles.
formulaChecks.grating: Adjacent-slit phase agreement requires g sinθ=mλ. With 500 lines/mm, g=2 µm; λ/g=0.25, θ1=14.4775121859°, y1=0.2581988897 m at L=1 m. |m|=4 is grazing and cannot hit a finite screen; no universal grating-minimum rule is inferred.
formulaChecks.singleSlit: Uniform-aperture amplitude integration gives I/I0=[sin(πu)/(πu)]², u=b sinθ/λ. Nonzero integer u are zeros. Differentiation gives tan(πu)=πu for nonzero secondary extrema; independently solved first positive maximum u=1.4302966531242025 and I/I0=0.04719044922581128.

checks: Exactly two open slits; the d dimension ends at both aperture centres, not at aperture edges.
Normal parallel incident arrows; the dashed geometric leg and horizontal reference have the same origin at the midpoint between the slits.
O lies on the central bright m=0 stripe, P on the upper bright m=+1 stripe, y is measured O to P, and L is measured between aperture and screen planes.
Dark minimum pointer lies between bright orders 0 and +1; the ±1 bright stripes are symmetrically placed within hand-drawn precision.
All visible phase, path-difference and screen formulas match the stated far-field idealization without envelope.
Independent exact geometry gives first bright positions ±5.000015625 mm and nearest dark positions ±2.500001953 mm, supporting the displayed rounded values.
cosmeticNotes: The non-scale sketch caption is duplicated. This introduces no scientific contradiction and is not a blocker.

checks: Six open apertures are present; the enlargement identifies g between adjacent aperture centres.
Textual principal-maximum condition, finite-screen grazing limit and all displayed numerical values are correct.
The caption limits the illustration to selected principal maxima and does not claim that secondary maxima are absent.
blockers: P is at the upper ray endpoint around screen y≈516 px, whereas the y1 arrow and m=+1 designation terminate around y≈570 px. These are different points, so the geometry does not identify one consistent measured maximum.
Rays drawn from different apertures end at different upper screen heights (approximately 516 and 568 px, with the dashed line between them) rather than the same principal-maximum observation point.

The extra Δs double arrow measures a transverse separation between a ray and the dashed geometric line, not the optical path-length difference along propagation. This is incompatible with the displayed Δs≈g sinθ interpretation.
reviews.requiredRepair: Use one unambiguous geometric midpoint-to-P leg and measure y1 from O to that same P. Remove the invented Δs transverse measure or replace it with a correct path-difference construction. All contributing rays intended to meet at P must actually meet there.

checks: Exactly one aperture; b measures the gap between its two edges.
The minima formula excludes m=0, the centre is a central maximum, and the first-minimum pairwise-cancellation statement is correct.
All printed screen-position formulas and rounded example numbers are correct: first minima ±5.000015625 mm, central width 10.000031250 mm, first secondary maxima ±7.151528985 mm.
The horizontal intensity axis has equally spaced unique ticks -2,-1,0,+1,+2, and zeros occur at the stated integer locations.
blockers: The intensity plot uses a single I/I0 axis with baseline near y=1412 px and unit peak near y=1042 px. The dashed line labelled 0.047 and the first side peak lie near y=1371 px, about 0.11 of the central height, not 0.047. No separate expanded side-lobe scale is declared.
The first drawn positive side peak is near x=1088 px, while u=0 is near x=728 and u=1 near x=970: u≈1.49, nearly the half-order explicitly warned against, not the stated u≈1.43.

The screen is drawn obliquely in perspective and the L endpoint, O and vertical y1 measure use different projected references, despite the requested flat 2D geometry. The defective intensity scale is independently sufficient to block.
reviews.requiredRepair: Generate the actual sinc-squared curve on one correct linear intensity scale, with first side maximum u=1.430296653 and height 0.047190449. Keep zeros at integer u and all labels tied to the actual plotted locations. Use one flat screen line with consistent O, first minimum, y1 and L references.
